summary: The Latin of Pliny's section on lands the sea has taken away. In 2.205 he says the sea took lands "first of all where the Atlantic is, if we believe Plato". The older English chapter numbers are 2.90-2.92 (Bostock and Riley). Latin only: no clean public-domain English text was available.

tree.title: Pliny, Natural History 2.204-2.206 (older numbering 2.90-92): islands made and lost; lands taken by the sea "if we believe Plato"
tree.summary: Pliny lists islands nature has split off or joined to the mainland. In 2.205 he says the sea took away land "first of all where the Atlantic is, if we believe Plato", over a vast area, then lists drowned lands, then Helike and Bura in the Gulf of Corinth.
